Pendulum Squat

The pendulum squat is a plate-loaded machine squat that allows a deep, upright squat pattern. The pendulum arc keeps the resistance path natural and reduces spinal loading compared to barbell squatting.

How To Perform

  1. 1 Stand on the platform with your back against the pad and shoulders under the shoulder pads.
  2. 2 Position your feet hip-width apart on the angled platform.
  3. 3 Release the safety and squat down as deep as your mobility allows.
  4. 4 Drive through the feet to return to the starting position.

Form Cues

  • ✓ Keep chest tall throughout the movement.
  • ✓ Drive knees out over the toes.
  • ✓ Full depth — aim for thighs parallel or below.

Common Mistakes

  • ✗ Rising up on the toes at the bottom.
  • ✗ Knees caving inward.
  • ✗ Partial range of motion.
💡 Professor Splits Says:

Progressive overload is the engine of muscle growth. Track your weights and aim to add small increments weekly. For Pendulum Squat, this means gradually increasing load, volume (sets × reps), or decreasing rest periods over time.

FAQ

How many sets of Pendulum Squat should I do?▾
3–4 sets of 8–15 reps is a solid starting point. Adjust based on your training frequency and overall weekly volume for quads. Beginners should start with the lower end; advanced trainees can push toward the upper range.
What muscles does Pendulum Squat target?▾
Pendulum Squat primarily targets the Quads. Secondary muscles include Glutes, Hamstrings.
Is Pendulum Squat good for beginners?▾
Pendulum Squat is beginner-friendly. Focus on technique with lighter loads before adding weight.
How much rest between sets?▾
For Pendulum Squat, 2 min of rest between sets is recommended. Compound exercises require more recovery — longer rests (2–3 min) allow better performance on the next set.
